meta.title: Purchase refunds | Lenix Protocol
meta.description: Open a refund case for a lost, damaged, delayed, or misdescribed purchase. We review the trail first. You pay a share of what is recovered, not of what you claimed.
meta.keywords: purchase refund, lost parcel claim, damaged shipment, delayed delivery, buyer refund, seller refund, Lenix Protocol

Hero.title: Recover value from lost, damaged, and failed purchases
Hero.description: Submit the order, the payment proof, and what went wrong. We check whether a claim against the carrier, marketplace, or counterparty is recoverable. Instant payout, if any, comes after underwriting. Refunds are not guaranteed.
Hero.imageAlt: Investigator reviewing a purchase dispute file

System.title: One file for what a carrier or counterparty still owes
System.description: Some refund platforms connect to a merchant carrier account and watch every label. Lenix does not. You open a case. We review it, build the pack, and follow it until it settles or we close it in writing.

review.title: Review before anyone files
review.description: Payment trail, tracking, photos, and the claim window the carrier or marketplace actually published. If the window is already closed, we say so.

file.title: Prepare, then send
file.description: The desk drafts the claim from your evidence. Nothing goes to a carrier, marketplace, or counterparty until you accept the terms.

track.title: A case file, not a live tracker
track.description: Status, evidence, and what came back sit on the case. You get written updates. We do not ingest every shipment from your carrier login.

fee.title: Fee on recovered value
fee.description: The recovery fee is a share of money that actually returns. Intake is free. If nothing comes back, you do not pay that fee.

Split.title: Stalled parcels that usually get written off
Split.description: When tracking stops and nobody has time to sit in a carrier portal, the loss sits on the books. If the claim window is still open, that is a recovery file: tracking, declared value, photos, and the service you paid for.

points.lost: Lost, no-scan, and return-to-sender, where the contract still covers the goods or the postage.
points.damaged: Damaged on arrival, with photos and a date that still fits the carrier's deadline.
points.late: Late against a paid delivery guarantee, where the tariff actually pays compensation.
points.manual: A buyer reports a missing order. You add it by hand. We do not need a carrier API to start.

Split.imageAlt: Parcel tracking records used as claim evidence

Cases.title: The shortfalls we take
Cases.description: Buyers and sellers can open the same intake. The desk routes the claim to the party that still owes the value.

lost.title: Lost in transit
lost.description: No delivery scan, stuck in a depot, or marked delivered when the buyer never received it. Tracking and the payment proof go in the file first.

damaged.title: Damaged on arrival
damaged.description: The box landed, the goods did not survive. Photos, packing, and the order value matter more than a long complaint.

delayed.title: Late against a guarantee
delayed.description: You paid for a timed service. The parcel missed it. Compensation depends on the carrier's published window, not on how angry the buyer is.

short.title: Not as paid for
short.description: Wrong size, empty box, never shipped. This is a counterparty claim, not a stolen-wallet case. Payment proof still has to match the order.

Process.title: How a refund case runs
Process.description: The same four-phase recovery process we use on lost-asset cases, applied to a purchase that missed or a parcel the carrier still owes.

assessment.title: Initial assessment
assessment.description: We check the payment trail, tracking, the counterparty, and whether the claim window is still open. No money moves here.

strategy.title: Refund strategy
strategy.description: Written terms: instant or after-return, who carries the gap if the item never comes back, and the fee on recovered value.

coordination.title: Active coordination
coordination.description: If instant is approved, the buyer is paid first. The item still has seven days to ship. We follow the carrier or marketplace claim in parallel.

return.title: Verified payout
return.description: Funds go to a verified wallet, or the case closes with a written reason. We do not reverse the original card sale.

Boundaries.title: What this desk does, and what it will not
Boundaries.description: A complete claims page says both. If your case sits on the wrong side, we will point you elsewhere instead of taking the file.

items.a: Lost, damaged, delayed, or misdescribed purchases with a payment trail.
items.b: Seller claims against a carrier or marketplace while the published window is still open.
items.c: Buyer cases where the other party stopped answering after the goods fell short.

items.a: Connect to your carrier account and scan every label. You open the case.
items.b: File Visa or Mastercard chargebacks. We are not the merchant of record on the original sale.
items.c: Handle stolen or drained wallets. That is recovery services.

Fees.title: You pay a share of what comes back
Fees.description: Intake does not bill a recovery fee. After assessment we send terms. The fee is a percentage of recovered value, not of the amount you claimed. If the case recovers nothing, that fee is zero.

points.intake: No setup charge to open a file.
points.share: Fee only on recovered funds, never on a rejected claim.
points.terms: Nothing is filed, and no payout is sent, until you accept the terms in writing.

Faq.title: Before you submit
Faq.subtitle: Straight answers on monitoring, payouts, and fees.
Faq.discuss: If this is a lost-wallet case, use recovery services instead.

types.question: What can I file here?
types.answer: Lost, damaged, delayed, empty, or misdescribed purchases. Buyers and sellers use the same form. Stolen crypto is a different desk.

monitor.question: Do you watch all of my shipments?
monitor.answer: No. Some refund platforms connect to carrier accounts and flag every stalled label. Lenix reviews the cases you submit. If you have a tracking number and a payment proof, that is enough to start.

instant.question: Do I get the money back in seconds?
instant.answer: Not at submit. Instant payout is an underwriting decision after we score non-return risk. Many cases wait for the return or for the carrier to pay. We will not pretend otherwise.

fees.question: What do you charge?
fees.answer: A share of recovered value, agreed in writing before we file or pay. Intake is free. If nothing is recovered, you do not pay that recovery fee.

chargebacks.question: Will you reverse my card payment?
chargebacks.answer: No. We do not represent chargebacks to Visa or Mastercard. The original merchant of record stays in place. This desk recovers value through the carrier, marketplace, or counterparty, then pays a verified wallet if the case clears.

timeline.question: How long does a case take?
timeline.answer: Assessment is due within one business day. Carrier and marketplace claims then follow their own windows, often two to six weeks. You get a written estimate after review.

evidence.question: What should I attach?
evidence.answer: Payment hash or invoice, tracking, photos of damage if you have them, and any chat with the other party. PDF, JPG, PNG, or WebP, 8 MB max. A case can start without a file. Weak evidence just slows the claim.

guarantee.question: Do you guarantee a refund?
guarantee.answer: No. Closed claim windows, missing proof, and counterparties who will not pay all fail. We close those in writing instead of keeping the file open for show.
